bullets.title: SNDK: Massive investor day catalyst — 100% FCF return pledge, HBF tech, LTAs drive 14-25% surge
bullets.body: SNDK surged 14-25% after its investor update where management committed to 100% excess cash return to shareholders, guided long-term non-GAAP gross margins ~80% and EPS ~75% through 2030. JPMorgan resumed at Overweight citing AI inference-driven NAND inflection; the company signed 8 LTAs worth ~$94B total contract value at ~80% GM floor pricing. NAND TAM is seen inflecting from ~$70B in CY25 to $300B+ in CY26 and $500B+ in CY27, with data center share flipping from ~30% to ~50%; HBF technology (8x CapEx efficiency vs HBM) is in consortium with META, GOOG, and Hynix with 2027 samples and 2028 production.

bullets.title: NVDA: Morgan Stanley neocloud revenue-share backstop could add 10-25%+ to EPS/EBIT; UBS sees $15+ CY27 EPS
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Joe Moore details NVDA's neocloud backstop structure: at 25GW scale generating $500B in rental revenue, NVDA capturing ~25% at 100% margin could drive 25% FY29 EBIT upside; even a 2-5GW deployment yields ~10% EPS uplift. UBS separately models NVDA beating its July-quarter by $3-4B and guiding October-quarter to $107-110B, with a path to $15+ CY27 EPS and nearly $20 CY28 EPS. Blackwell demand remains supply-constrained and Rubin is arriving sooner than expected.

bullets.title: WDAY: +18% on Silver Lake M&A speculation; SaaS M&A screen refreshed
bullets.body: WDAY surged 18% on Reuters reports of Silver Lake acquisition talks, generating unusual options volume of 31,413 contracts (332% above average). Morgan Stanley's MS TMT note refreshed a SaaS M&A screen of 70%+ GM names under $50B EV. UBS notes core WDAY demand is stabilizing but sees limited near-term AI upside; analysts caution against chasing given PE hesitancy and need for strategic buyers.

bullets.title: RDDT: Joins S&P 500 on August 18, +15% premarket on index inclusion
bullets.body: Reddit (RDDT) will join the S&P 500 on August 18, driving shares up ~10-15% in premarket trading. One source notes an existing position in RDDT.

bullets.title: AAPL: App Store moat cracking on Supreme Court ruling; partners with BABA on China LLM; iPhone 18 price hikes $100-300
bullets.body: The Supreme Court denied Apple's stay on the App Store commission ruling, making alternative app stores/side-loading increasingly likely and threatening Apple's 15% fee on out-of-store purchases. Separately, Apple partnered with Alibaba to develop and train an LLM for the China market (shift away from third-party models). iPhone 18 is expected to see price hikes of $100-300 despite lower OLED display costs ($68 vs $110-120 for Pro Max), and Apple is exploring multi-year content licensing for Siri improvements.

bullets.title: DIS: MS flags as long idea with new CEO, 23-42% upside, D23 catalyst this week
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley presents DIS as a long idea with CEO D'Amaro simplifying and monetizing; base PT of $125 implies ~20% upside (15x FY28 EPS of $8.35) with a bull case adding another ~22% upside. Key drivers: domestic parks attendance +3%, per-capita spend +4%, DTC streaming path from ~10% to 20%+ EBIT margin, and the D23 fan event this week as a near-term catalyst. The MS media recap also flags NFLX and SPOT favorably for 2H.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: Wells Fargo upgrades FOXA to OW/$80 PT on ROKU acquisition synergies
bullets.body: Wells Fargo upgraded Fox Corp to Overweight from Equal Weight and raised its PT to $80 from $65 following Fox's announced deal to acquire Roku. The firm expects ~$300M in ad revenue synergies within 24 months and notes NFL contract risk is reduced as no changes are likely before 2030. FOXA was up 2.5% premarket on the news.

bullets.title: TMUS: Wolfe downgrades to Peer Perform on competitive pressure, capex, and management uncertainty
bullets.body: Wolfe Research downgraded T-Mobile to Peer Perform from Outperform, removing its prior $236 PT. AT&T and Verizon are aggressively competing in postpaid, Starlink V3 threatens fixed wireless, management departures and DT merger rumors create uncertainty, and CEO is signaling 6G/broadband capex likely exceeding the $20B+ 'flexible capacity' guide. TMUS is down 11% YTD vs S&P +14%; Wolfe sees the historical +2x NTM EBITDA premium as no longer justified.

bullets.title: LITE/COHR: JPMorgan bullish post-earnings — LITE NPO revenue tracking $50-100M in C4Q26, EML backlog through 2029
bullets.body: JPMorgan's 'Chips for Breakfast' note flags LITE as a key idea: CEO framed NPO as TAM-expander with ~6 meaningful engagements; revenue tracking to $50-100M in C4Q26 and crossing $100M in C1Q27, with demand upside skewed toward scale-up in 2H27. EML backlog is covered through 2027 with negotiations extending into 2028-2029 at generally higher prices. COHR results were noted alongside LITE post-earnings declines that offset memory gains.

bullets.title: AMAT: Beat and raised but -6% on elevated expectations; Wolfe and JPM see $25-28 CY28 EPS as durable
bullets.body: Applied Materials guided F4Q to $10.25B (vs ~$9.60B consensus), with Semi Systems guided up to >30% Y/Y growth. Its largest customers now provide detailed 8-quarter demand forecasts extending to 2030. However, shares fell ~6% as near-term gross margin was seen as flat q/q — a 'show-me' story — and expectations were elevated. Wolfe and JPMorgan both see CY28 earnings power of $25-28 supporting 19-21x valuation; JPM raises PT to $660 noting AGS expected to exceed 20% Y/Y in CY26.

bullets.title: MU: Up 3.9% premarket on Micron Ventures' $250M AI fund and New Street Research upgrade
bullets.body: Micron rose 3.9% in premarket trading after Micron Ventures launched a $250M AI investment fund and New Street Research upgraded the stock. The broader memory sector is recovering after July's unwind, with non-TMT L/S funds buying at ~2.3x the rate of TMT-focused funds.

bullets.title: NVDA Feynman roadmap: Accelerated 2H28 timeline, upgraded A16 process and custom HBM
bullets.body: NVDA is accelerating development of its Feynman architecture for 2H28 with an upgraded A16 process node, increased SoIC 3D stacking, and custom HBM. News about no CPO in Feynman had been circulating since June/July. AMD's Rosa processor faces competitive pressure if it fails to deliver.

bullets.title: DLR: HSBC upgrades to Buy with $240 PT as AI data center demand firms
bullets.body: HSBC upgraded Digital Realty Trust to Buy with a $240 price target. The Anthropic-Riot deal (20-year, $9.1B lease for 191MW at Rockdale) and Fermi's 15-year/222MW TensorWave lease signal a firming AI data center market. Anthropic is targeting 10GW of compute online in the next couple of years.

bullets.title: RIOT/WULF/HUT: Powered shell sector weak on cost-of-capital; RIOT confident on Corsicana LOI
bullets.body: Powered shell providers are facing weakness from rising cost of capital (credit spreads, equity costs) and interconnection delays. RIOT management expressed confidence in its Corsicana LOI (6-month timeline to lease), targets $11-12/watt capex, and expects an IG backstop for Rockdale near-term. ERCOT Batch Zero uncertainty could benefit larger operators like RIOT. HUT and WULF are viewed as relatively defensive; hedge funds were modestly net buying HUT last week.

bullets.title: NFLX: Pershing Square discloses new position per activist summary
bullets.body: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Inc. disclosed six new investments including Netflix (NFLX), SPGI, ICE, ALC, MA, and V. No size or thesis was disclosed in the filing beyond the position itself.

bullets.title: SHOP: Trading -3% in Canada premarket amid broader market rotation
bullets.body: Shopify's Canadian listing (SHOP.CN) was trading down 3% (C$214.35, -C$6.62) in mid-morning Canadian trading, underperforming the flat TSX composite. No specific news catalyst was cited beyond general market rotation.

bullets.title: BE: Oppenheimer bullish on Bloom Energy — stack life improvement to 5+ years drives margin and demand upside
bullets.body: Oppenheimer is constructive on Bloom Energy (BE): stack life improved from ~9 months at IPO to 5+ years, substantially reducing service costs. Demand is diversifying across data center and C&I (~2/3 of 2024 install base), with 200-300MW/qtr capacity adds at Fremont supporting a ~5GW demand path. Margin upside comes from renewed ITC and reduced need to pass all cost reductions to customers.

bullets.title: HD: Q2 earnings Aug 18; consensus +0.9% comps, $4.73 EPS; options imply ~4.7% move
bullets.body: Home Depot reports Q2 results on August 18. Consensus expects +0.9% US comps and $4.73 EPS vs guidance range implying $14.69-$15.28 for the full year. JPMorgan's retail sales read-through suggests a potential upside surprise: 1Y data implies +3.0% US comp vs Street +0.9%, though 2Y is flat. HD is up 14% since May vs S&P +5.3%. Options price ~4.7% move.

bullets.title: INTU: UBS sees consensus too optimistic on FY27 growth; channel checks show softness
bullets.body: UBS is below consensus on Intuit, modeling 12.4% FY27 GBSG growth vs the Street's ~14%. Channel checks show softer Payroll, Money, and Mailchimp trends with fading pricing tailwinds. UBS is not making a formal rating change but flags this as a 'show-me' situation.

bullets.title: FWONK/TKO/LYV: MS media 'Live 5' — FWONK Top Pick, TKO upgraded to OW, LYV at 52-week high
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Sean Diffley media recap designates Formula One (FWONK) as Top Pick, upgrades TKO Group to Overweight, and includes Live Nation (LYV) as a 'Live 5' idea. LYV also hit a new 52-week high (up 18.6% YTD). DIS and NFLX are flagged as long pitches with upside drivers into 2H.
